# Company

`sales.obj.core.company` · v1.0.0 · **draft** · scope **core**

> The organisation as an entity in the world — firmographics, structure, market position, technology. Objective and externally verifiable, independent of whether we have ever spoken to them. It is what ICP fit is scored against. Every field here would be true if our company did not exist: headcount, industry, ownership, installed technology, fiscal year-end. Nothing about how the relationship is going belongs here — that is Account. The practical consequence is that a Company record can be enriched, scored and disqualified before any human contact, which is the entire basis of targeting; and that when the relationship turns, none of these fields change, which is exactly why they must not be stored in the same place as the ones that do.


Also called: `Organisation`, `Firm`, `Legal Entity`

## Constraints

- **`co.no_relationship_fields`** Company carries no field describing our relationship.Owner, stage, health, ARR and renewal live on Account without exception.
- **`co.identity_on_domain`** Two records sharing a primary_domain are the same companyand must be merged. Name equality is never sufficient.
- **`co.subsidiary_no_inheritance`** A subsidiary inherits no firmographic from its parent.Structure is inherited; scale is not.
- **`co.stale_never_raises_fit`** Firmographics past the freshness horizon may lower a fitscore and may never raise one.
- **`co.fit_is_scored_here`** ICP fit is computed against Company only. A fit score thatreads any Account field is measuring the relationship and calling it targeting.


## Business rules

- **`co.domain_is_the_key`** Company identity resolves on primary_domain, never on name. Names change on rebrand and acquisition and collide across jurisdictions; the domain survives both and is present in every email address already held.

- **`co.no_relationship_state_here`** No field describing our relationship — owner, stage, health, ARR, renewal — may be stored on Company. Every one of them belongs to Account. This is the rule that keeps expansion distinguishable from new business.

- **`co.stale_data_cannot_raise_fit`** Firmographics past their freshness horizon may lower an ICP fit score but never raise it. Asymmetric on purpose: a stale disqualifier is probably still true, while a stale qualifier is how a company that halved in size stays in the enterprise segment.

- **`co.subsidiary_scores_on_its_own_numbers`** A subsidiary's fit is scored on its own firmographics. The parent's revenue is not the subsidiary's budget, and inheriting it produces a pipeline full of enterprise deals being run by a forty-person business unit.

- **`co.regulated_implies_a_security_gate`** A company with any entry in regulatory_regimes will run a security review. A close plan that does not allow for it is not optimistic, it is wrong about the date.

- **`co.contraction_outranks_fit`** headcount_trend = shrinking must override a strong firmographic fit. Companies in contraction start evaluations and finish very few of them, and the pipeline they generate is the most convincing kind of waste.

## Actions

- **Resolve the company to a domain** (system) — The prerequisitefor everything else here. Every enrichment provider keys on domain, and every deduplication depends on it.
- **Refresh firmographics** (system) — Cheap, and the only defence againstfit scores computed from a headcount that has since halved.
- **Score fit against the ICP** (system) — Runs against thisobject alone. If it needs anything from Account, the ICP definition has leaked relationship state into a targeting model.
- **Map the corporate group** (human) — Parent, subsidiariesand which entity actually signs. Discovering at contract stage that the signing entity is in another jurisdiction costs weeks.
- **Identify the installed incumbent** (human) — Convertsan assumed greenfield sale into a displacement. Different discovery, different objections, different timeline anchored on their contract end date.
- **Disqualify on firmographics** (human) — The cheapest actionin the entire domain, because it costs one decision and saves a quarter of activity. Doing it before contact is the whole point of separating Company from Account.


## Evidence

- **document** · 9500 bp — Statutory filings and registers. Definitive onstructure, ownership and fiscal year-end; silent on everything commercial.
- **contract** · 9000 bp — The signing entity and jurisdiction, stated bythem. Arrives far too late to help with targeting.
- **website** · 7500 bp — Positioning, jobs and detectable technologies.Uniquely, this is the strongest source that is available before contact.
- **crm** · 6500 bp — Existing record. Whoever typed it did so once, on aday nobody remembers.
- **meeting_transcript** · 6500 bp — They describe their own structure. Accurateabout intent, imprecise about numbers.
- **manual_entry** · 5500 bp — Researched by a person. Good on the day itwas written and undated thereafter.
- **derived** · 3500 bp — Structure inferred from review functions and dealsize. Corroborating only, and always overridden by enrichment.


## Metrics

- **enrichment_coverage** (percent) — Share of companies with firmographics fresherthan the horizon. Bounds the trustworthiness of every fit score downstream.
- **duplicate_rate** (percent) — Companies sharing a primary_domain across records.The direct cost of resolving identity on name.
- **icp_fit_predictive_power** (percent) — Correlation between fit score and eventualwin rate. If this is near zero the ICP is describing who we sold to, not who we should sell to.
- **disqualification_lead_time** (days) — Days from identification to disqualification.Every day here is spent on a company that was never going to buy.
- **firmographic_drift** (percent) — Share of records whose employee_band changedon refresh. Sets the freshness horizon empirically instead of by opinion.
- **cycle_length_by_structure** (days) — Median cycle split by legal_structure.The evidence behind the structural_complexity weighting.


## Examples

- **220-person private SaaS firm, Series B, growing** — The clean fit. One economic buyer,no procurement function, a fiscal year-end nobody has mentioned yet and which will decide the quarter.
- **40-person subsidiary of a 30,000-person listed group** — Scores enterprise on inheritedfirmographics and buys like a small business — except for the parent's procurement policy, which applies in full. Wrong on both size and speed unless parent_company_ref is populated.
- **Regulated healthcare provider, 3,000 staff** — regulatory_regimes populated. A securityreview is certain, not probable, and the close plan must contain it from day one rather than absorb it in week nine.
- **Declining incumbent-heavy retailer, shrinking headcount** — Strong firmographic fiton paper. headcount_trend = shrinking should override it — they will run the evaluation and finish nothing.
- **Company record carrying account_owner and health_score** — THE classic conflation. Themoment a relationship field lands here, expansion becomes indistinguishable from new business and every churned company drops out of the target list it still belongs in.

> Four of eleven patterns are executable and all four are weak, because the substrate is deal-scoped by construction while this object is true before any deal exists — every executable pattern here infers a company fact backwards from a conversation we are already in, which is the wrong direction for a targeting object. The highest-value signal gap by a distance is contact.email_domain: every message already ingested carries the company's only durable natural key in its From header and it is discarded, so records cannot be deduplicated, enrichment cannot be keyed, and accounts link to companies only by a hand-typed name. It is also the cheapest item in the backlog and it unblocks the entire enrichment chain behind it. Second is hiring_surge, the strongest pre-deal timing signal in the profession and one of a whole class L2 cannot express, since every observation kind it emits presupposes an open conversation.
